For those interested: A (failed?) Proof of Concept on improving close-ups with Neural Enhance upscaling.

MP4 if you want to have a better look at it. SendVid compression isn't great.

https://mega.nz/#!sU4H2DDJ!rpBp0ntWVFVQMXoGUMRSk6DEon-gQYI8G_T8GeHOsMc

Introduction:

For those who don't know, Neural Enhance is a model for predictive upscaling using deep learning.

I wanted to see if I could improve close-ups during merge by scaling the faces using Neural Enhance vs the default bicubic interpolation.

I would have wanted to compare how well the SRGAN upscaling model would work too, but the code available for that needed much more rewriting to splice into the merge process so I couldn't be bothered.

I also tried training my own model for NE using only high res faces, but I the results were unsatisfactory. Most likely because of limited training time and/or lacking dataset size (2000 images).

Results:

As you can see in the video, simply upscaling with NE does not give a noticable improvement.

However, using the NE-deblur model, it's possible to sharpen up the face a bit. Unfortunately, with that sharpness, comes artifacts. And although they can be remedied to some extent by applying a gaussian blur, you then have to worry about not blurring too much and losing the already small improvements you gained.

Now, I've only tested it on this one video, so there might be other cases where it would be more sucessful,.

I was hoping to see better results, but at least this was an interesting short project.
